title: Foreign Influence Transparency Scheme Amendment Bill 2019
short_title: Foreign Influence Transparency Scheme Amendment Bill 2019

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would expand foreign influence registration, reporting and disclosure requirements, including people producing material for public distribution on behalf of a foreign principal.
It would cover relevant activities undertaken before formal registration, consolidate disbursement reporting and clarify the fault elements of offences concerning registration or renewal failures.
The changes would begin the day after royal assent, with the expanded communications definition applying to arrangements existing before commencement as well as later arrangements.
changes: A person’s belief about a foreign principal’s intention could inform the assessed purpose of an activity.
Registrable communications would require disclosure even where the communicator had not registered.
Disbursements for a foreign principal would accumulate across voting and non-voting periods.
Threshold disbursement reports would generally be due within seven days during voting periods and 14 days otherwise.
Unregistered people could report covered activities when applying for registration.
summary.affected: People conducting registrable activities for foreign principals, producers and distributors of relevant material, and foreign principals are affected.

speeches.speaker: Mark Dreyfus
speeches.brief: The Foreign Influence Transparency Scheme Amendment Bill 2019 closes loopholes in the existing Act by amending definitions of communications activity, clarifying intent provisions, fixing reporting obligations, and aligning offence provisions. The speaker supported the changes while criticising the government's drafting process.
